judgment.notes: Reviewed all four uses of the conditional M001 statement. A001 takes both factors to the kth time component, with derivatives (u_t)_k; A002 takes u_k and (u_t)_k, with derivatives (u_t)_k and (u_tt)_k; A003 takes both factors to u_k on the jth spatial coordinate line; A004 takes u_k and (u_j)_k on that line, with derivatives (u_j)_k and (u_jj)_k. In every case scalar field and algebra are R, so all normed-field/ring/algebra premises hold for the standard real structures. H002 supplies the requisite derivatives, D003-D006 identify them, and BG002 checks component passage. At r>0 the time extensions agree locally with the original curves (BG005), so no derivative at or across zero is needed. For spatial applications the coordinate is x_j and time is fixed positive. M001 yields exactly the component-product derivatives used; BG003-BG006 cover finite sums and differentiation of the constant identities. There are no E applications.

S001 converts H004 to sum_k u_k^2=1 (BG001), differentiates componentwise by M001, and obtains 2(u·u_t)=0, hence F001. The identity is universal in point and positive time, so differentiating it in S003 is legitimate. S002 uses the H005 witness only algebraically and F001 to get u_t·(u_tt-Δu)=0. S003 differentiates F001 to obtain |u_t|^2+u·u_tt=0, and differentiates the unit constraint along a spatial coordinate twice, establishing the first spatial orthogonality identity at every point before differentiating it again. This yields |u_j|^2+u·u_jj=0 without exchanging mixed derivatives. In S004, u·u=1 and F003 give a=u·(u_tt-Δu)=-|u_t|^2+sum_j|u_j|^2; substitution proves the pointwise equation. All sign changes and dot-product identities are finite real algebra. BG001-BG006 positively check only routine norm/component/sum/locality/constant/uniqueness details. No measure or integration property is used. For n=0 the spatial sum is empty and the spatial universal clause is vacuous; for m=0 H004 is inconsistent but the conditional computations still hold and no nonempty-coordinate assumption was used.

scope: Coverage is reviewer-reported; reading alone is not mathematical assessment.
